newsitem.title: USA: Dow may continue to sell certain assets.
newsitem.headline: Dow may continue to sell certain assets.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said Thursday it will continue to identify and may sell assets that do not meet profit goals.

"As part of Dow's aggressive management of its portfolio, the company will continue to look for the best value-creating opportunities for its businesses, including selling certain assets which do not meet its economic profit objectives," the company said in a year end statement.
Dow did not identify any specific assets.

Dow reported 1996 yearend earnings from continuing operations rose to $1.9 billion or $7.71 a share from $1.88 billion or $7.03 a year ago. There were about 22 million fewer shares outstanding in 1996. Sales for all of 1996 totaled $20.1 billion, near its record 1995 sales of $20.2 billion.

Through a combination of volume growth, improved productivity, business portfolio restructuring and lower costs, Dow said it was able to offset almost $1.2 billion of the approximately $2 billion impact of receding prices and higher feedstock and energy costs.
As a result, Dow said its operating income for 1996 was $3.1 billion, off only $804 million from the previous year.

During the year, Dow sold or restructured its interest in a number of businesses including: Boride Products, Crestar Energy Inc and Cynara. In addition, the company realized a pre-tax gain of $77 million for the fourth quarter and $120 million for the year through the sale of a portion of its ownership in Oasis Pipeline, contributing to a total of $343 million of sundry income for the year.
